title: Basal-Omni: An open-weight 31B model for AI decision-making (nr 1 on JevBench)
content:
Instructions to use Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra with libraries, inference providers, notebooks, and local apps. Follow these links to get started.
- Libraries
-  Transformers How to use Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra with Transformers: # Use a pipeline as a high-level helper
from transformers import pipeline
pipe = pipeline("text-generation", model="Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra")
messages = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image", "url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/p-blog/candy.JPG"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "What animal is on the candy?"}
        ]
    },
]
pipe(text=messages) # pip install -U transformers accelerate
# Load model directly
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra")
model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained("Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra", device_map="auto")
messages = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image", "url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/p-blog/candy.JPG"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "What animal is on the candy?"}
        ]
    },
]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
	messages,
	add_generation_prompt=True,
	tokenize=True,
	return_dict=True,
	return_tensors="pt",
).to(model.device)
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256)
print(processor.decode(outputs[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:]))

basal-omni-1.0-ultra (experimental)
basal-omni-1.0-ultra (31B) is the largest model of basal-omni, basal's line on Google Gemma 4. It is an experimental release: it is trained on text decisions only, and it also answers the same questions about images, read by Gemma 4's own image encoder without media training (zero-shot; media training comes in the next releases). The 31B base has no audio encoder, so this tier takes no audio. It answers the same typed questions as basal-1.5, over the same API.
What it is. Inspired by System 1 (fast, intuitive) decision models such as Jev. Instead of writing an answer,
the model reads a state (a message, a document, retrieved passages, an agent trace, a web page as JSON). It then
answers a typed question about it (choice, yes/no noul, score, and in the basal engine multi, act and
tool; a tool question over OpenAI or MCP tool definitions picks the tool, not its arguments). The answer is a
calibrated probability for each allowed answer, in one forward pass, without generating text. The answer never
falls outside the options you give, and the probability says how sure the model is.
What is new against basal-1.5-max.
- A Gemma 4 base (31B) instead of Bielik (11B).
- Up to 255 options per question (basal-1.5: 10).
- One option order by default (basal-1.5 averaged two).
- Images in the same request ("media", served with --media on), zero-shot; no audio.
- Trained on about 640,000 Polish and English typed decisions, with soft targets from basal-1.5.
Results
Served with the basal engine: basal-omni-1.0-ultra on one H200 and basal-omni-1.0-max on one H100, both with --mode eager, bf16, one option order; basal-1.5-max as released (--mode fast, both option orders). Same items and the same clients for all three. Measured with basal 2.0; basal 2.1 gives the same top answer on 23,278 of 23,278 served-check rows.
- Against basal-omni-1.0-max: ahead on PL decisions (+2.5 points, 95% interval +2.0 to +3.1), the English corpus test of 1,479 items (0.751 vs 0.724, +0.6 to +4.7) and the English external panel (+6.9 points over its items; ahead on 9 of 10 tasks: WinoGrande 0.863 vs 0.710, BIG-Bench Hard 0.883 vs 0.809, JudgeBench 0.700 vs 0.600; behind on FinancialPhraseBank, 0.947 vs 0.967). Level on Polish general knowledge (+1.3, 0.0 to +2.7) and PL-Real (−0.7), whose intervals include zero.
- Against basal-1.5-max: PL decisions +3.9 points (+3.3 to +4.5), Polish general knowledge +2.6 (+1.1 to +4.1), English corpus test 0.751 vs 0.659, English panel +11.8; level on PL-Real (+0.3).
- ¹ Coverage: per question type, at 0.47% observed error (max: 47.4% at 0.47%). A type without a certified threshold is deferred: at the 1% target, score questions go to a person. basal-1.5-max's 62.2% used one threshold pooled over all types; under that rule this model reaches 77.5% at 0.75% error.
- Werdykt v1: 0.879 (95% interval 0.871–0.887; Polish 0.881, English 0.877), 5.6 points above basal-omni-1.0-max (0.823) and 10.6 above basal-1.5-max, served with --deterministic on one H200 (one request per forward). Ahead of max in all 10 categories; weakest categories: rules (0.550; compute exact thresholds and dates in code), contracts (0.822) and long documents (0.854).
Quick start
1. Install into a fresh uv environment:
uv venv --python 3.12 --allow-existing ~/basal-env && source ~/basal-env/bin/activate
uv pip install torch==2.11.0 torchvision==0.26.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
uv pip install "basal[media] @ https://github.com/rkinas/basal/archive/refs/tags/v2.1.0.tar.gz"
2. Start the server. It prints basal: model ... ready:
basal-serve --model Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra --mode eager --media on --port 8000
This release runs in the engine's eager mode only (PyTorch, bf16, about 62 GB of GPU memory for the weights; on one 80 GB GPU, states up to about 10,000 tokens, see Limitations). The fast mode
(shared prefix, CUDA graphs), the FP8 checkpoints and the MLX / GGUF ports of basal-1.5 come with a later release of
this line.
3. Ask questions, exactly as with basal-1.5:
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": "Klient: od wczoraj nie mogę zalogować się do bankowości internetowej, system pokazuje błąd hasła.",
  "questions": {
    "dept":   {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Do którego działu skierować zgłoszenie?",
               "criteria": {"cards": "Reklamacje kart", "online": "Wsparcie ba

report.summary: Basal-Omni 1.0 Ultra is a 31B open-weight model built on Gemma 4 that answers typed decision questions with calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass, claiming first place on JevBench.
report.background: Mainstream LLM design assumes a model writes an answer, often with a reasoning trace. A smaller counter-current — inspired by "System 1" thinking — treats inference as classification: read a state (a message, document, retrieved passages, agent trace or web page as JSON), then pick among predefined options with a calibrated probability. Jev popularised this pattern, and the open-source basal line has been building it in public: basal-1.5 ran on an 11B Bielik base, aimed mainly at Polish. This release moves to Google's open Gemma 4 31B weights. The appeal is practical: a single forward pass instead of long generation, output that cannot drift outside the allowed options, and a probability that says how confident the model is — useful for triage, routing, judging and tool selection where abstaining to a human is better than guessing.
key_points: No text generation at all: instead of writing an answer, the model reads a state and answers a typed question (choice, yes/no, score, multi, act, tool), returning a calibrated probability for each allowed option in one forward pass. The answer can never fall outside the options you supply.

Bigger base and far more flexibility: Gemma 4 (31B) replaces basal-1.5's Bielik (11B), supported options per question rise from 10 to 255, and a single option ordering is now the default. It was trained on roughly 640,000 Polish and English typed decisions, using soft targets distilled from basal-1.5.

Measured gains over its predecessor: ahead of basal-omni-1.0-max by 2.5 points on Polish decisions, and by 6.9 points on an English external panel (WinoGrande 0.863 vs 0.710, BIG-Bench Hard 0.883 vs 0.809, JudgeBench 0.700 vs 0.600), scoring 0.879 on Werdykt v1. It trails on FinancialPhraseBank (0.947 vs 0.967).

Images work zero-shot, audio does not: requests can include images read by Gemma 4's own image encoder despite no media training, an explicitly experimental feature. The 31B base has no audio encoder, so this tier accepts no audio. The model also handles tool questions over OpenAI or MCP tool definitions, choosing the tool rather than filling its arguments.

Heavy serving footprint: only eager PyTorch bf16 mode is available, needing about 62 GB of GPU memory for weights and one 80 GB GPU for states up to roughly 10,000 tokens. Fast mode, FP8 checkpoints and MLX/GGUF ports are promised for a later release, so laptop-class experimentation is not yet realistic.
report.impact: The release is a strong signal for the 'decision layer' pattern: rather than prompting a frontier model to classify, route or judge, you call a small specialised model that returns bounded options plus a confidence score. That matters most where errors are expensive and abstention is a feature — banks, insurance, moderation, agent control — because calibrated probabilities with per-type error thresholds let systems escalate to a human instead of confidently guessing. For developers it offers an HTTP endpoint and native tool-selection over OpenAI/MCP definitions, which can replace fragile structured-output prompts. The catch is operational: 62 GB of weights, eager-mode-only inference and no quantised or MLX/GGUF builds yet make it a server-side tool, not a laptop one, and throughput will lag optimised generative stacks until fast mode ships.
report.tools: To follow up, start with the basal engine (github.com/rkinas/basal, v2.1) and the Hugging Face repo Remek/basal-omni-1.0-ultra, which ships recipes for Transformers, vLLM, SGLang and Docker Model Runner. Compare against the lighter basal-1.5 line if you need FP8, GGUF or MLX builds for smaller GPUs. For evaluation, look at Werdykt v1 and JevBench, and test tool routing using the OpenAI and MCP tool-definition inputs rather than argument generation.
